sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Multidisciplinary Assessment
sections.description: This section guides the learner through the initial encounter with a pregnant patient presenting with atypical abdominal symptoms. It details the specific history taking, physical examination findings, and the immediate stabilization efforts required when managing complex masses in pregnancy.
subtopics: Recognizing atypical symptoms: Severe abdominal pain and dyspnea in the second trimester
Physical examination nuances: Differentiating uterine enlargement from extra-uterine masses via palpation
Initial vital sign stability vs. symptom severity (VAS scoring)
The role of multidisciplinary teams (Obstetrics, Surgery, Radiology) in early triage
Management of concurrent complications: Urinary tract infection and anemia

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Imaging Strategies and Safety Protocols
sections.description: Focusing on the diagnostic algorithm, this section explains why specific imaging modalities are chosen over others during pregnancy. It highlights the utility of Ultrasound and Non-Contrast MRI while explicitly addressing safety contraindications regarding radiation and contrast agents.
subtopics: Primary role of Ultrasound with Color Doppler: Identifying vascularity and cystic nature
Advanced imaging with Non-Contrast MRI: Determining mass boundaries, solid/cystic composition, and relationship to the uterus
Safety considerations: Why Gadolinium is avoided and magnetic field strength limitations
Interpreting imaging findings: Distinguishing between decidualized endometriomas and cystic degeneration of leiomyomas
Limitations of imaging in obscured anatomy due to 'steric bulk' of the gravid uterus

sections.section_title: Biochemical Markers and Differential Diagnosis Formulation
sections.description: This section addresses the interpretation of tumor markers in a physiological context. It teaches learners how to distinguish between malignant indicators and benign physiological elevations (like CA-125) during pregnancy to avoid false-positive diagnoses.
subtopics: Physiological fluctuations of CA-125 across trimesters versus pathological elevation
Utility and limitations of other markers (CA 19-9, CEA, LDH) in pregnancy
Constructing the differential diagnosis: Benign vs. Malignant etiologies for large pelvic masses
Deciding factors for malignancy suspicion based on marker trends rather than single values
Correlating imaging characteristics with biochemical data to narrow down origins
